title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted II
summary: Given an integer array, determine the maximum number of chunks that can be created such that sorting each chunk individually and concatenating them results in a sorted array.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the maximum number of chunks that can be created such that sorting each chunk individually and concatenating them results in a sorted array.
constraints: Split arr into the maximum number of nonempty contiguous chunks.
Sorting every chunk independently and concatenating must equal the globally sorted array.
Duplicates and negative values are allowed.
hints: Compare each original prefix with the same-length prefix of sorted(arr).
Maintain their running sums and cut whenever the sums match.
The sorted prefix contains the globally smallest values, so an equal sum is possible only when the two prefix multisets agree; every such independent boundary should be used.
editorial: The sorted prefix contains the globally smallest values, so an equal sum is possible only when the two prefix multisets agree; every such independent boundary should be used.

tests.explanation: No proper prefix contains the same values as the corresponding globally sorted prefix.
The array can be divided into four valid chunks.
